title: Investigate and patch tenant rollout–induced KV prefetch thrashing
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Over the last three customer escalations (two Dedicated clusters, one Private on-prem rollout) we've observed repeated bursts of long-context tail latency and temporary queue starvation correlated with tenant rollout/drain events. Root cause appears to be a prefetch/admission race: maintenance-driven drain signals + canary traffic cause many long-context requests to requeue while the continuous batcher aggressively prefetches KV state for the same tenants, thrashing the host KV cache and triggering repeated eviction/rehydration cycles. This amplifies latency for short/medium requests and causes customer-visible timeout spikes.

Why this is unique: unlike previously-seen admission-window skews, this case is triggered by coordinated maintenance/rollout events (rolling upgrades, node drains) and manifests across hosting modes because the control-plane propagation of maintenance flags is delayed or dropped in some Private network topologies. The continuous batcher currently assumes relatively stable admission signals; transient rollouts violate that assumption and expose hysteresis and prefetch overshoot.

Goal: implement a safety net that prevents prefetch-driven KV thrash during tenant rollouts without regressing throughput for steady-state workloads. Provide immediate mitigation for currently impacted customers, a durable fix in runtime-1.24, and a smallset canary rollout plan for Private clusters.
mitigation_steps: Apply emergency tenant-prefetch cap (soft limit) on affected hosts — hotpatch running runtime in Dedicated clusters
Enable maintenance-propagation flag in edge-router for Private customers to accelerate drain signals to batcher
Temporarily lower prefetch concurrency for tenants flagged with recent requeues (30s window) via config toggle
Customer comms: notify impacted customers that a targeted mitigation was applied and offer guided Dedicated/Private canary for final fix
proposed_fix_summary: Introduce per-tenant prefetch budget with decay/hysteresis to avoid immediate re-prefetch after eviction
Add a maintenance-aware admission fence: if a tenant is in active drain/upgrade window, hold aggressive prefetch for that tenant until drain completes
Add KV eviction telemetry: per-tenant eviction rate, average KV rehydrate latency, prefetch-backoff events
Router-level maintenance propagation: reliable propagation of maintenance state to local batchers in Private networks (gRPC backoff + persistent subscription)
verification_steps: Unit tests for prefetch budget accounting and decay behavior
Integration test: synthetic mixed-length workload with simulated node drains validating no KV eviction spike and short-request P95 stable
Staging canary in a Dedicated pool with heavy mixed tenant mix for 48 hours
Private canary with 1 customer on isolated network, monitoring evictions and tail latency
rollout_plan: 1) Apply hotpatch mitigation in impacted Dedicated clusters (immediate). 2) Merge runtime-1.24 fix branch behind feature flag. 3) Canary rollout to a single Dedicated pool for 48h. 4) Enable feature-flag in Hosted tier for low-traffic region for 24h. 5) Coordinate Private on-prem canary with customer success + SRE, enable after green signals. 6) Gradually remove feature flag after 2 weeks of stable telemetry.
monitoring_and_alerts: New alert: per-host KV-eviction-rate > 10/min sustained for >2min
New SLO erosion signal: short-request p95 latency increase >25% vs baseline for >5m
Incident playbook addendum: if rollback needed, disable prefetch budget and revert maintenance propagation change
rollback_plan: Feature-flag off to restore previous behavior; apply increased admission throttling as stopgap; rollback hotpatches if instability observed. Inform customers and open follow-up RCA ticket.

2026-03-09 - QA (Diego Alvarez): Integration test harness added to CI with drain simulation. Found regression when prefetch budget decay was too slow; adjusted decay window from 120s -> 30s.
2026-03-12 - Product (Anika Shah): Customer success messaging drafted for impacted customers; recommend offering private canary slot for 2 customers.
2026-03-14 - Luca Romano: PR opened: runtime:prefetch-budget + maintenance-propagation. Runbook and dashboards attached. Requesting review from infra and privacy teams before enabling in Hosted.

2026-03-14 - Security (Jun Park): Quick review - no secrets involved but Private propagation changes will need encryption checks in next security pass. Marking security_review_required for release branch as true.
